summary: The imaging archives hold live-cell screens, fixed-cell screens and raw EM volumes separately, with fixation recorded as a protocol detail rather than an experimental variable; no public dataset found pairs the same cells live and after coagulating fixation and scores fine cytoplasmic texture against organelles. IDR exposes 'Imaging Type: fixed cell imaging' (128 images) and BioStudies has one study (S-BIAD1137) imaging a marker in both live and fixed cells, which is the closest match.
next_step: Compile a correlative live/fixed test set: pick IDR or BIA studies that image the same cell line live and fixed with the same cytoplasmic marker (start from S-BIAD1137), record fixative per study, and define a texture score; alternatively locate a published CLEM study that deposited both live frames and post-fixation EM of the same cells.
obstacles_confirmed: Precisely matched live-to-fixed cells are less common than unmatched images: no such paired dataset surfaced in seven searches.
Modern fixation methods differ from those Thompson criticized: archives record formaldehyde/glutaraldehyde/cryo, not the coagulating fixatives (sublimate, picric, osmic) of 1917.
Cell Image Library exposes no API we could query, so its content could not be confirmed.
